unit.title: Inception & “Build Just Enough Process”
unit.moc: the 4 core terms — the core principle — what it does/doesn't — the 7-step loop — the name

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 1 — gate
checkpoint.prompt: Reproduce the 4 core terms and the core principle, and name what the tribunal is NOT. Write a short verdict.

facts.text: **the Living Tribunal** is a system for answering one hard question by running several independent AI models against it. A sitting opens with a single problem and closes with a single verdict.

The four names exist so every stage has one unambiguous word: **A Sitting** is one problem run, **Quorum** is the vote (3 to 5 models), **Convergence** is the final verdict. Mixing up 'the vote' with 'the answer' is the classic beginner error.

In practice the `hub` CLI drives the whole run: hand it one brief and it routes the brief to independent lanes, collects their votes, and records the Convergence. The model is just the engine inside one lane.
A common slip is calling the model 'the tribunal'. The model is one witness doing the reasoning; the tribunal is the courtroom around it - lanes, votes, and the converged verdict.

exercises.prompt: One problem run through the tribunal is called:
The multi-model vote over that problem is:
Match each term to its meaning.

lessons.title: Core Principle: Build Just Enough Process

facts.text: **Formalize Thinly** means writing down just enough process to enforce three habits: independence, grounding, and a recorded dissent. Anything past that is machinery, not value.
Discipline is the point because it survives model swaps: a thin process lets you change lanes or models without rebuilding a bureaucracy. The habit of challenging and citing carries the value.
The whole system fits in four artifacts: this document, the intake template, the ledger, and the `hub` CLI. If it is not one of those four, it is not part of the system.

The habit already paid real dividends: it caught an AI's wrong Cloudflare/Prisma/Neon claims, audited a session report, and shipped a migration blueprint. Few tools get that much real-world validation.
'Just enough' does not mean 'less rigor': the rigor lives in gates instead of heavy build-out. The checkpoint at the end of this unit is exactly such a gate.

exercises.prompt: Formalize Thinly means the value is ___ , not the machinery.
Which of these is NOT part of “the whole system”?
The tribunal's habit has already caught a wrong model claim and audited a session report.

lessons.title: What the Tribunal Does (and Doesn't Do)

facts.text: The tribunal takes a problem from any session and returns ONE converged, evidence-cited answer. That single artifact is the whole product.

It routes the SAME brief through 2 to 5 independent model lanes, forces them to challenge each other, and grounds the result in the second brain plus fresh docs. Independence plus grounding is what turns opinion into something you can defend.
What comes back is a verdict or a blueprint, not commits: citation-backed text that a human then acts on in the real repo.
It is deliberately NOT a build environment, a chat playground, an agent orchestrator for long-running work, a replacement for reading primary docs, or a destination for lab data or secrets.

exercises.prompt: Which is a true statement about what the tribunal returns?

options: a way to route the same brief to independent lanes
grounded in the second brain + fresh docs
a build environment that returns commits
a way to force lanes to challenge each other

exercises.prompt: Which statement VIOLATES the tribunal's stated scope?
exercises.scenario: A new team member proposes using the tribunal as a destination for lab data and secrets.
options: grounding the result in the second brain
routing the same brief to independent lanes
storing lab data and secrets with the tribunal

lessons.title: The 7-Step Loop: Intake → Triage → Ground → Route → Converge → Verify → Record

facts.text: Every run walks seven steps in order: Intake, Triage, Ground, Route, Converge, Verify, Record. Intake is the problem arriving; Record is the verdict filed.
Independence is the product of the loop: each lane sees the SAME brief, and no lane sees another's output until convergence. Blind routing is what makes the vote honest.
Verify means checking against the artifact the user actually runs: run it, grep the repo, read the vendor doc. Model agreement alone never counts.
Record closes the loop by writing down what was decided. In the learn path, clearing this unit's checkpoint is that step made visible: your verdict becomes permanent.

exercises.prompt: Put the 7 loop steps in order.
What does “verify” mean in the loop?
options: checking against the artifact the user runs

lessons.title: The Name: Quorum — Why It Was Chosen

facts.text: `Quorum` is the name because a quorum of independent voices - not one model - is the property that makes the hub work.
Real Claude proposed it precisely for that reason: the word names a decision rule, not a vibe. Enough independent agreement is what lets a verdict count.
`Crossbench` was the runner-up in the same naming round.
Do not read 'quorum' as a headcount feature of the CLI. It is the principle that a verdict only counts when several independent lanes converge on it.

exercises.prompt: Which name was recommended, and why?
options: PolyModel Hub — because it is generic
Quorum — because it names the independence property
Sounding Board — because it is evocative

exercises.prompt: The name “Quorum” was proposed by real Claude.
